(b) A RESOLVER GRAMMAR THAT FIRST READ NAMES FROM ANY CLAUSE. The first form of the re-binding read every name in a parenthesis holding axiom words: KLSilence :86 read UNBOUND on "List", where "kept axiom-free" is said of the headed recursion, and Voice7 :124 and TriviumCode :9 read on "DERIVES" and "SIDE". (c) BACKTICKS SPLIT ACROSS A LINE. The rerun bank first carried a quote wrapped over two lines, each with odd backtick parity; rejoined by a later commit (relay c025820e).
(d) A HEREDOC THAT COLLAPSED A BACKSLASH. A scratch diff script for the seam's overlay passed through a bash heredoc lost a backslash and failed to parse; written again by the Write tool.

(e) A SOURCE MISREAD IN A GLOSSARY ENTRY. The HINGE-order entry first said b638's entry was the definition the census at v0.6 counted under; data/glossary.txt :81 says v0.7. Corrected before the commit.

(f) THE NAVIGATOR'S: A READ-FIRST CITATION OF A FILE NEVER WRITTEN. The ferry cited data/b650_closing.txt; b650's ferry ordered no closing record. The author's word: the navigator's error; b650's weight cited from its trail record and entry.

(g) THE NAVIGATOR'S: A RE-CUT WRITTEN AS IF A CELL ANSWERED A BLOCK. (R261)(7)'s "re-cut to the ACTION cell's sentence" assumed a cell answering the block; the cell answers a row, and many rows' ACTION answers one sentence (row 7, ConservationBridge :9). The author's word: the navigator's.

(h) THE NAVIGATOR'S: A RULE THAT ASSUMED SENTENCE ROWS. The answer that followed assumed the bank graded sentences; b647's SIDE-kernel table grades blocks (its bank :3). The author's word: the navigator's.

(i) THE NAVIGATOR'S, AS THE SEAT READS IT: A RESOLVER REPAIR ALREADY IN PLACE. (R261)(4) asked the resolver to bind a docstring claim to the declaration the docstring heads; it already did (tools/axiom_claim.py :255-:263 before the edit), so the edit as worded could not turn rows 2 and 5; raised to the author, who ruled the re-binding.

(j) THE NAVIGATOR'S, AS THE SEAT READS IT: A ROW COUNT. (R261)(8) names "the 33 OVERREACHES and UNDERSTATES rows"; the bank holds 33 OVERREACHES and 6 UNDERSTATES. All 39 printed (relay data/b651_navigator_rows.txt).

(k) THE SEAT'S: A COMMIT HASH READ FROM THE WRONG END OF A LOG. The step-zero bank and the worklist first named relay 78e850cd (the ferry's commit) as the push-out commit; git log -2 prints newest first, and the push-out commit is 2afbd48e. Corrected before the seal (relay 0cba15d1).

(l) THE SEAT'S: A SUITE ARM WHOSE POSITIVE CONTROL PASSED. G-RESOLVER-COUNTS's first control popped the last row of the after bank, a MENTION its predicate does not count, so the mutated copy still passed; caught by the mid-act run (relay data/b651_checks_mid1.txt) and repaired to change a CONTRADICTED row's verdict before the seal (relay f133eaf5).

(m) THE SEAT'S, IN THE SEALED RECORD TOOL: A TRAIL HEAD LOOKED UP UNCONVERTED. TRAIL_HEAD carries a backtick possessive ("the largest kernel`s docstrings"); the guarded route lands it converted to a typographic apostrophe, and the sealed trail route looked the line up unconverted, so its bank read line None. The trail landed whole at OPEN_TRAILS :13874; the seat wrote data/b651_trail.json by hand with the line found by the converted head, the sealed tool unedited. Found after the trail record was written, so the record's defect line lists (a)-(l).

(n) THE SEAT'S, IN THE SEALED SUITE: FIVE ARMS READING THE RECORD BY THE WRONG CONVERSION. G-FINDINGS-ENTRY, G-TRAIL-RECORD, G-TRAIL-CARRIES-ROOT, G-TRAIL-CARRIES-SEAL and G-NEXT-ACT-NAMED look the entry's title and the trail's head up through b566_record's poss, which renders a backtick possessive as a straight apostrophe; the record was landed through b641_record's _poss, which renders it typographic, and both texts carry one. The five fail at the close, pre-push and post-push alike. Read again with the landing conversion in place of the suite's (a scratch run, the sealed suite unedited), all five pass: the entry at FINDINGS :8229 and the trail at OPEN_TRAILS :13874 are as the record tool wrote them. Undeclared on the face; found at the pre-push run.
